documentation: Run free-form data queries (DQL) against PostgreSQL from a workflow and get rows back as JSON objects. Read-only by default: the pool sets default_transaction_read_only=on, so PostgreSQL rejects any write. The first argument is the SQL; the rest bind to $1, $2, … (never interpolated). Not the `store` KV backend — see mhl-store-postgres.

properties.name: dsn
properties.documentation: Full connection string (URL or libpq keyword/value). Use env("DATABASE_URL"). Wins over the discrete fields.

properties.name: user
properties.documentation: Role name. Prefer a least-privilege, SELECT-only role.

properties.name: password
properties.documentation: Role password. Use env("PGPASSWORD"); the host resolves and redacts it.

properties.name: sslmode
properties.documentation: libpq sslmode: disable | prefer (default) | require | verify-ca | verify-full.

properties.name: read_only
properties.documentation: Default true — sets default_transaction_read_only=on so writes are rejected by PostgreSQL, and `exec` is disabled. Set false to allow DML via `exec`.

properties.name: max_rows
properties.documentation: Maximum rows a single `query` may return before it errors (guard against unbounded SELECTs). Default 10000; 0 = unlimited.

properties.name: statement_timeout
properties.documentation: Per-statement server-side timeout as a Go duration ("10s", "500ms"). Unset = server default.

properties.name: log
properties.documentation: Optional path to append a JSON-lines wire trace (SQL head + arg count, never values) for debugging.

methods.name: query
methods.documentation: Run a SELECT; every row is an object keyed by column name.

methods.name: queryRow
methods.documentation: The first row, or null when the query yields none.

methods.name: queryValue
methods.documentation: The first column of the first row, or null.

methods.name: exec
methods.documentation: Run a single DML/DDL statement, returning the affected-row count. Errors unless read_only is false.

methods.name: execScript
methods.documentation: Run a multi-statement DDL/DML script in ONE transaction (all-or-nothing). No bind parameters. Errors unless read_only is false. Use `exec` for statements that cannot run in a transaction (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, VACUUM, CREATE DATABASE).
